payload.label: Apply an amount across rows of another list
payload.job: Work out how the amount one row holds (a payment, a credit, a grant) goes across the open amounts of rows of another list (invoices, bills, budgets) as allocation rows, propose it first, answer allocations to take back, or read what is applied and open on a row
payload.description: action propose works out, writing nothing, how the source row's amount would go across the targets in an order (oldest_first by default, or as read-data/list-settlements.json orders say) and what is left unapplied as a credit. apply answers one allocation row per target (source, target, amount, date, request) for the allocations list "<source>-to-<target>-allocations" under `keep`, for the caller to store; give items [{ target_id, amount }] or leave them out to apply the proposal; request_key makes it apply once. Every item is answered done, already_done or refused with why, and the outcome says all, some or none. remove answers allocation_ids as rows to take away under `keep`, reopening exactly those targets once stored. position reads one row ({ row: { row_id, amount_field }, role, allocations: { list_id } }): its amount, applied, open and the allocations behind it. A row with no amount is refused: empty is not zero. Body: lists (the rows read), source { row_id, amount_field }, targets { list_id, amount_field, order_field?, row_ids? }, order, allocations { list_id?, *_field? }.

list_id.description: The list in the request: the source (or the lines, or the row's list) when the body leaves its own list_id out.

lists.description: The lists the action names, as the caller read them from a store: each { id, row_type, fields, ...the list's own definition, rows: [{ id, values }] } with every row the action reads. The run keeps nothing; what to store comes back as `keep`.

keep.description: Present when something is to be stored: { lists: the list definitions made, rows: [{ list_id, row_type, id, values | null }] } where values is the whole row and null takes the row away.

payload.label: Reconcile lines against a statement
payload.job: Work out closing a set of cleared lines against a statement with any difference explained in words, answer a receipt of each close, find lines changed or removed after they were closed, and answer the undo of the last close
payload.description: action close takes lines { amount_field, closed_in_field? }, row_ids, period, opening_balance, statement_balance, request_key and residual_reason when the lines do not add up to the statement; it answers each line marked closed and the receipt for "<lines>-reconciliations" under `keep`, for the caller to store. The same request_key returns the same receipt; a line already closed elsewhere is refused. check lists every line that changed or was removed after its close (record: true answers each as a discrepancy row to keep, once). undo answers the lines of the latest close reopened and its receipt marked undone; the receipt stays. Give the lists in `lists`.

payload.label: Post entries whose lines add to zero
payload.job: Check an entry of signed lines adds to zero and answer it to keep, once per entry id, answer its undo as a new entry with every line negated, and list every entry in the lists that does not add to zero
payload.description: action post takes lines { amount_field, group_field }, entry_id and rows [{ values }] (two or more); lines that do not add to zero are refused and nothing is answered to keep; the same entry_id posts once. reverse takes entry_id and reverse_id and answers the negated lines to keep; the original lines stay. Both answer the rows under `keep` for the caller to store; give the lists in `lists`. balance reads every line and answers the entries that do not add to zero and the lines with no amount or no entry (unplaced, never counted as zero). It reads only.

payload.label: Total the lines of a quote or invoice
payload.job: Total the lines of a quote or invoice in order, where each percent line names the base it multiplies (the line above, the lines since the last subtotal, or all above) and a subtotal line resets that base
payload.description: action totals takes lines { kind_field?, value_field?, base_field?, order_field? } and row_ids or every row. A line's kind is a row of read-data/list-settlements.json line_totals.kinds (amount, percent, subtotal); a percent line must name its base. Answers each line with its amount, the base it used and the running total, and the total. It reads only the `lists` handed in.

payload.label: Report on an accrual or a cash basis
payload.job: Read the same rows on an accrual basis (by the date each row is due) and on a cash basis (by the date of each allocation to it) for a period, each figure naming its basis and the rows behind it
payload.description: action basis takes targets { amount_field, date_field }, allocations { list_id }, from, to and basis (accrual, cash or both; the list's saved report_basis, else both, when left out). Answers each basis asked with its total, count and the rows behind it (capped, with truncated said). It reads only the `lists` handed in.
